ai.literal: Having investigated, without showing favoritism, desiring impartiality, towards anyone, having deliberated, doing [justice] indeed is the way of a righteous reign.
ai.translation: To investigate a matter thoroughly, to show no favoritism, to lean only towards absolute impartiality, and to deliver judgment after careful deliberation is the true path of justice.
ai.modern: ஒரு குற்றத்தை நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து, யாரிடமும் பட்சபாதம் காட்டாமல், நடுநிலைமை தவறாமல், சட்டங்களை நன்கு ஆலோசித்துத் தண்டனை வழங்குவதே முறையான ஆட்சியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the core duties of a ruler or judge in maintaining a righteous reign. First, they must fully investigate the facts of a case without rushing to judgment. Second, they must remain completely unbiased, refusing to let personal relationships or status influence their view. Third, they must lean only towards absolute impartiality, and finally, they must consult the laws and deliberate carefully before delivering a verdict. Following these steps is what defines true justice.

ai.literal: All the world that lives looking towards the sky, the subjects live looking towards the king's sceptre.
ai.translation: Just as all living beings in the world look up to the sky for rain to survive, so do subjects look up to the righteous sceptre of their king for their livelihood.
ai.modern: மழைக்காக வானத்தை எதிர்பார்த்து உலகத்து உயிர்கள் எல்லாம் வாழ்கின்றன; அதுபோல, அரசனது செங்கோலை எதிர்பார்த்து அவனுடைய குடிமக்கள் வாழ்கின்றனர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the dependence of the world on rain to the dependence of citizens on a just ruler. The word 'வான்' refers to the sky, representing the rain that sustains all life on earth. 'கோல்' refers to the sceptre, symbolizing the king's righteous and just rule. Just as crops and living beings cannot survive without timely rain from the heavens, citizens cannot thrive or live in peace without the protective and fair governance of their ruler. The parallel structure of 'வானோக்கி வாழும்' and 'கோல் நோக்கி வாழும்' beautifully highlights this vital relationship.

ai.literal: To the scriptures of the righteous and to virtue, as the foundation, stood the king's sceptre.
ai.translation: The sceptre of a just king stands as the very foundation for both the sacred scriptures of the wise and the virtue of the world.
ai.modern: அறிஞர்களின் நூல்களுக்கும் அறத்திற்கும் அடிப்படையாக விளங்குவது மன்னனின் செங்கோல் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of just governance in preserving society. The poet states that the sceptre of the king ('மன்னவன் கோல்') stands ('நின்றது') as the ultimate foundation ('ஆதியாய்') for both the sacred scriptures of the wise ('அந்தணர் நூற்கும்') and the practice of virtue ('அறத்திற்கும்') in the land. Without a just ruler to maintain order and protect the people, neither spiritual wisdom nor moral conduct can survive or flourish. Thus, the rule of law is the prerequisite for all higher human pursuits.

ai.literal: Embracing the subjects, wielding the sceptre, the great earth's king, embracing his feet, will stand the world.
ai.translation: The world will stand embracing the feet of the great king who wields his sceptre of justice while embracing his subjects.
ai.modern: தன் குடிமக்களை அரவணைத்துச் செங்கோல் செலுத்தும் பெரிய நிலத்து மன்னனின் அடிகளைப் பற்றி இவ்வுலகம் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the reciprocal relationship between a ruler and the people. When a king rules with compassion, embracing and protecting his subjects (kuti talii) while maintaining a just administration (kol occum), he wins their absolute loyalty. In return, the people of the world will willingly embrace and follow his feet (ati talii nirkum). The poet beautifully repeats the word 'talii' (embracing) to show that a ruler's embrace of his people is met with the people's embrace of his authority.

ai.literal: In the country of the king who wields the sceptre according to justice, rain and harvest will gather together.
ai.translation: In the land of a king who wields his sceptre in accordance with justice, both timely rain and abundant harvests will always come together.
ai.modern: நீதிநெறிப்படி செங்கோல் செலுத்தும் அரசனுடைய நாட்டில், மழையும் விளைச்சலும் ஒருங்கே கூடி நிலைபெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the direct connection between a ruler's just governance and the prosperity of the natural world. The term 'இயல்புளி' means 'according to the established path of justice', and 'கோலோச்சும்' refers to wielding the sceptre of authority. In the country ('நாட்ட') of such a righteous king, both rain ('பெயலும்') and agricultural yield ('விளையுளும்') will gather together ('தொக்கு') in abundance. The poet suggests that nature itself responds harmoniously to a just administration, ensuring that the land never suffers from drought or famine.

ai.literal: Spear is not victory giving-thing; king's sceptre, and that, bends not if.
ai.translation: It is not the spear that brings victory to a king, but his sceptre of justice, provided it does not bend.
ai.modern: மன்னனுக்கு வெற்றியைத் தருவது அவனுடைய வேல் அல்ல; அவனுடைய செங்கோல் கோணாமல் நேர்மையாக இருக்குமானால், அந்தச் செங்கோலே வெற்றியைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that a ruler's true strength lies in justice rather than military might. The spear represents physical weapons and army strength, which are declared insufficient on their own to secure victory. Instead, it is the sceptre, representing the administration of justice, that brings true and lasting victory. The crucial condition is that this sceptre must not bend, meaning the ruler must remain completely unbiased, fair, and unswerving in upholding the law.

ai.literal: The ruler protects the world all; him justice protects, without failing if he administers.
ai.translation: The ruler protects the entire world; and if he administers justice without failing, that justice itself will protect him.
ai.modern: அரசன் உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லாரையும் காப்பாற்றுவான்; அவன் தன் செங்கோல் ஆட்சியைத் தடையின்றிச் செய்வானானால், அந்த நீதியே அவனைக் காப்பாற்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the reciprocal relationship between a ruler and the justice they administer. While the ruler's duty is to protect all the people of the world, the ruler's own safety is secured by their adherence to justice. If the ruler administers justice ('முறை') without any failure or lapse ('முட்டாச் செயின்'), that very justice will serve as a shield to protect them. Thus, the ultimate protector of a sovereign is not their military might, but their own righteous governance.

ai.literal: He who is easy of access, not investigating and not doing justice, that king, by an easy state, himself will perish.
ai.translation: A king who, though easy of access, does not investigate and administer justice, will fall from his position and perish easily of his own accord.
ai.modern: எளிய அணுகுமுறை உடையவனாக இருந்தாலும், வழக்குகளை ஆராய்ந்து நீதி வழங்காத அரசன், வலிமையிழந்து தானாகவே எளிதில் அழிந்துபோவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of active justice in governance. While being easy of access (எண்பதத்தான்) is a virtue for a ruler, it becomes meaningless if he fails to investigate grievances (ஓரா) and deliver fair justice (முறைசெய்யா). A king who neglects these core duties will lose his authority and fall to a low, vulnerable state (தண்பதத்தான்), perishing of his own accord (தானே கெடும்) without the need for a powerful external enemy.

ai.literal: Protecting the subjects' welfare, guarding and cherishing them, punishing crime is not a blemish; it is the king's duty.
ai.translation: To guard and cherish the welfare of his subjects, and to punish crimes, is not a blemish on a ruler; it is his duty.
ai.modern: மக்களைப் பாதுகாத்து, அவர்களைப் பேணி வளர்த்து, குற்றங்களைத் தண்டிப்பது அரசனுக்குப் பழி ஆகாது; அது அவனுடைய கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core responsibility of a just ruler. A king must actively protect his citizens (காத்து) and nurture their well-being (ஓம்பி). When he administers justice by punishing crimes (குற்றம் கடிதல்), it should not be viewed as an act of cruelty or a moral blemish (வடு அன்று). Instead, punishing wrongdoers is an essential duty (தொழில்) required to maintain order and safeguard the innocent.

ai.literal: Punishing the wicked with execution by the king is equal to removing weeds from the green crop.
ai.translation: A king punishing wicked criminals with the death penalty is equal to removing weeds to protect a green crop.
ai.modern: கொடியவர்களைக் கொலைத் தண்டனையால் அரசன் தண்டிப்பது, பசிய பயிரில் உள்ள களைகளை நீக்குவதற்கு ஒப்பானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the king's duty of punishing severe criminals to a farmer weeding his field. The word 'கொலை' here refers to execution or the death penalty, and 'ஒறுத்தல்' means punishing. Just as weeds must be removed from a green crop ('பைங்கூழ்') to allow the plants to grow healthy, extremely wicked people ('கொடியார்') must be eliminated to protect society. The comparison highlights that capital punishment, when applied justly to the truly wicked, is not an act of cruelty but a necessary act of preservation for the welfare of the state.
